headline: Physics-based and deep learning models of cell mechanics and organization
label: Mechanics Of Cellular Organization
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair explicit mechanical or regulatory rules and measured parameters with spatially resolved cell organization outcomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference or simulation of cellular organization from explicit physical or regulatory rules. Bio-PINNs model cell-induced densification and tether formation in fibrous extracellular matrices using a near-to-far curriculum and deformation-uncertainty collocation sampling. BIOPOINT introduces deformable multi-particle nuclei and explicit ECM adhesive layers, calibrated to SKOV3 experimentally derived parameters. The neuroblastoma tumoroid study couples an agent-based model with a stochastic gene regulatory network to reproduce CD133+ stem cell spatial structure, implicating a short-range diffusive process. Shape2Fate works on the observational side, using morphology-aware deep learning to track endocytic and exocytic carriers in live-cell TIRF-SIM movies. What is new is the explicit linkage of mechanical or regulatory rules to spatially resolved outcomes, though scale, mechanism and validation differ across these studies.
